requirements.title: Rich terminal UI with native cursor and responsive hierarchy
requirements.acceptance: Native block cursor, gutter hierarchy, visible reasoning, formatted content, panel layout and bounded streaming are deterministic and tested.

requirements.title: ContextPatch model editing protocol
requirements.acceptance: apply_patch accepts contextual add/update/delete/move operations without hunk counts, applies transactions safely and separates strict unified diffs.

requirements.title: Host-neutral patch tool pack
requirements.acceptance: TUI, Chrome and isolated workspaces share one PatchToolPack and ContextPatch semantics through narrow host adapters.

requirements.title: Versioning and requirement traceability
requirements.acceptance: Every new requirement has unique identity, linked design and test documents, a target version, and a traceable commit message enforced by tooling.

requirements.title: Repository-level agent instructions
requirements.acceptance: Repository-level AGENTS.md makes requirement, version, commit, verification and release rules mandatory for every coding agent.

requirements.title: Host capability ports and composable coding workspace
requirements.acceptance: Host adapters expose probeable narrow ports and named application actions; profiles and capability graphs compose host-neutral coding tool packs; unavailable applicable actions degrade explicitly and cannot produce false completion evidence; no generic exec, Python, shell or binary runner is built in.

requirements.title: Portable workspace capsule and cross-host continuity
requirements.acceptance: A versioned, integrity-checked workspace capsule transfers project content, agent sessions and tasks, VCS/Git state, artifacts, evidence and environment requirements; import is staged and atomic, running resources are reconciled, host-sensitive state stays out of the agent namespace, and evidence is invalidated when the environment changes.

requirements.title: Portable Git backend with Git-compatible repository format
requirements.acceptance: PortableGitBackend is the default host-independent Git implementation and supports the common local Git subset over a workspace filesystem without a git binary; its objects, refs, HEAD and index interoperate with standard Git, while the CLI backend remains optional for advanced operations and conformance testing.

requirements.title: Architecture impact map and completeness evidence
requirements.acceptance: Architecture-impacting requirements enumerate providers, consumers, lifecycle, persistence, migration, observability and cleanup before coding, and cannot be verified without per-surface contract, integration and end-to-end evidence.

requirements.title: TUI host capability profile integration
requirements.acceptance: TUI and Headless share one workspace capability composition; Portable is the default shell-free Coding profile, Legacy is explicit, application Actions are configurable, Prompt derives from the actual registry, and completion requires current action or legacy execution evidence.

requirements.title: TUI workspace capsule export
requirements.acceptance: An idle TUI can export a flushed, non-empty Workspace Capsule with Ctrl+X or a fixed --capsule-export path; running sessions reject export without being silently stopped and failures remain visible and non-fatal.

requirements.title: Trusted application Action runtime with evidence
requirements.approvalNote: User explicitly authorized 2026-11-01 without claiming detailed review.
requirements.acceptance: Trusted local, native and remote providers expose stable named actions with schemas, probe state, approval, cancellation and structured results; TestReport conversion and current/stale evidence lifecycle remain owned by REQ-TEST-001.

adrReview.rationale: The action runtime is governed by the four-layer boundary, trusted leaf Action model, evidence-bound completion and rejected generic-exec alternatives.

requirements.title: Host baseline matrix and startup capability profiles
requirements.approvalNote: User explicitly authorized 2026-11-01 without claiming detailed review.
requirements.acceptance: Every host profile has a normative minimum matrix for core boot, portable workspace, portable coding and optional executable actions; startup probes fail missing baselines and degrade absent execution without replacing base ports with actions.

adrReview.rationale: The baseline matrix must preserve the Host Backend boundary and the rejection of representing every base capability as an Action.

requirements.title: Portable test discovery and TestEvidence lifecycle
requirements.approvalNote: User asked to continue the recommended 0.7.0 sequence without claiming detailed review.
requirements.acceptance: Test reports are structured and bound to workspace generation, file hashes, action version and environment; zero tests, malformed reports and stale evidence cannot complete a coding task.

adrReview.rationale: TestEvidence is a portable runtime concern constrained by current environment-bound completion.

requirements.title: TUI capsule import and streaming capsule v2
requirements.approvalNote: User asked to continue the recommended 0.7.0 sequence without claiming detailed review.
requirements.acceptance: TUI can preview and atomically import replace or merge capsules; capsule v2 streams compressed content-addressed partitions, survives interruption and rebinds or invalidates actions and evidence.

adrReview.rationale: Capsule v2 remains the sole cross-host transfer unit and must preserve portable repository semantics.

requirements.title: Language service and semantic code intelligence
requirements.approvalNote: User asked to continue the milestone sequence without claiming detailed review.
requirements.acceptance: Hosts can expose LSP-backed diagnostics, symbols, definitions, references and code actions through a language-neutral port with a portable text/symbol fallback.

adrReview.rationale: The design adds a language-service port and portable fallback within the existing layered architecture; it does not alter a durable cross-cutting rule or persistence format.

requirements.title: Subagent action isolation and fork-bound evidence
requirements.approvalNote: User asked to continue the milestone sequence without claiming detailed review.
requirements.acceptance: Child agents can call only actions compatible with their workspace binding and generation; parallel execution, cancellation, conflict detection and merge evidence are isolated from parent and sibling workspaces.

adrReview.rationale: Subagents remain configurable profiles with capability subsets and explicit workspace/action bindings.

requirements.title: Chrome shared capability composition and remote actions
requirements.approvalNote: User explicitly asked to proceed with Chrome composition implementation.
requirements.acceptance: Chrome runtime uses the shared capability composition, exposes browser and remote actions without shell fallback, and matches TUI/Headless tool schemas and evidence semantics.

adrReview.rationale: Chrome is a composition root and adapter, not a separate Core implementation; remote execution remains a named Action capability.

requirements.title: Windows Linux and iOS host baseline adapters
requirements.acceptance: Windows, Linux and iOS adapters satisfy the host baseline profiles, preserve portable coding without native processes and keep platform-specific path, execution and secret behavior outside Core.

adrReview.rationale: Cross-platform behavior depends on the portable-runtime-first decision and optional native interoperability backends.

requirements.title: Production coding benchmark fault injection and soak
requirements.acceptance: Multi-language benchmarks, fault injection and soak runs quantify completion, false completion, regression, repair cost, latency and manual intervention against release thresholds.

adrReview.rationale: Evaluation must measure current environment-bound evidence and false completion rather than historical or narrative claims.

requirements.title: Detailed design and user implementation authorization gate
requirements.acceptance: A requirement cannot enter implementation until it has detailed design and detailed test design, designStatus approved, and explicit user implementation authorization recorded in the registry.

requirements.title: Architecture Decision Record governance
requirements.acceptance: Durable architecture decisions use immutable ADR ids, a registered document set, user approval, bilateral supersede links, requirement traceability, and automated CI validation.

requirements.title: Agent-initiated decision intake and ADR triage
requirements.acceptance: Agents proactively capture durable discussion decisions in a DEC inbox, triage every new requirement for ADR needs, draft Proposed ADRs when architecture conditions apply, and cannot enter design approval or implementation with unresolved triage.

adrReview.rationale: The implementation applies the accepted agent-initiated decision intake and ADR triage rule.

requirements.title: Explicit unreviewed design approval
requirements.acceptance: Requirements may use approved_unreviewed only when the user explicitly authorizes implementation without detailed review and a non-empty approval note preserves that distinction.

adrReview.rationale: The implementation applies the accepted explicit unreviewed approval rule.

requirements.title: Action result approval and observability integrity
requirements.approvalNote: User asked to continue the recommended 0.6.1 hardening without claiming detailed review.
requirements.acceptance: Action result metadata and binary artifacts survive the tool and Session boundary, approval decisions produce durable receipts, required idempotency prevents duplicate side effects, late remote results are ignored, and TUI exposes a read-only Action manager.

adrReview.rationale: The hardening applies the accepted durable Action result and approval-record rule.

requirements.title: Extension manifest version synchronization
requirements.approvalNote: User explicitly requested the Chrome extension version display be fixed.
requirements.acceptance: Builds derive extension/manifest.json version from package.json, packaged and unpacked Chrome artifacts expose the same product version, and CI rejects version drift.

adrReview.rationale: The fix enforces the existing semantic-version source-of-truth rule without changing an architecture boundary.

requirements.title: Executable Side Panel settings UI contract
requirements.approvalNote: User approved writing the design and proceeding directly to implementation.
requirements.acceptance: Side Panel settings pages compose canonical settings primitives, the UI contract is discoverable without AGENTS rules, static and Chrome E2E checks enforce structure and computed styles, and requirement templates request UI impact evidence.

adrReview.rationale: ADR-016 selects component contracts and executable checks as the durable UI consistency mechanism.

requirements.title: Read-only execution debug hub and live event pull
requirements.approvalNote: User requested design, development and delivery according to the implementation standard.
requirements.acceptance: Agent execution events are normalized, redacted and emitted by outbound transport; a read-only Debug Hub persists and exposes cursor pagination, SSE streaming and NDJSON export; Chrome exposes configuration without listening on a port; external consumers can inspect live and historical execution.

adrReview.rationale: ADR-017 defines the outbound ingestion and read-only cursor-pull debug boundary.

requirements.title: Bounded streaming runtime and Browser memory
requirements.approvalNote: User reported approximately 11 GB browser memory usage and explicitly required a complete fix.
requirements.acceptance: Streaming updates use source projection deltas without recurring full history clones, Side Panel and persistence are bounded and coalesced, EventLog/network/debug/resident Session caches have explicit limits, and long Chrome tasks no longer grow memory with every token across the complete history.

adrReview.rationale: ADR-018 defines the bounded streaming and resident-memory invariants required by the P0 incident.

requirements.title: Chrome for Testing E2E baseline
requirements.approvalNote: User explicitly requested Chrome for Testing as the primary E2E browser.
requirements.acceptance: All Chrome E2E specs use one shared launcher; the default gate requires Chrome for Testing headless; headed CfT and explicit Stable Chrome profiles are available; missing CfT does not silently fall back to Stable.

adrReview.rationale: ADR-019 establishes Chrome for Testing as the canonical automated E2E baseline.

requirements.title: Layered host-neutral Agent prompt composition
requirements.acceptance: A deterministic assembler composes host-neutral Core, Workspace and Mode policies with isolated host policies, registry-derived capability context, bounded Skill/Profile instructions and runtime facts; every supported host has prompt golden and behavioral evidence without cross-host capability leakage.

adrReview.rationale: ADR-020 proposes a cross-host prompt composition boundary and must be approved before implementation.
